planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring in sharply drained, lean soil; cut back hard to 4-6 inches in early spring since flowers form on new wood.

directions: Summer Sorbet is a variegated sport of the classic blue mist shrub, with aromatic green leaves edged in bright golden yellow that hold their color through the heat of summer without scorching. Periwinkle-blue flower clusters appear along the upper stems from midsummer into fall, creating a striking two-tone effect against the gold-margined foliage. Grow in full sun and lean, well-drained soil; overly rich or moist conditions produce floppy, less colorful growth and invite root rot. Cut the whole plant back to a low framework each spring to encourage dense, compact regrowth and maximum bloom, and pair it with blue- or purple-flowered perennials to echo the flower color while the foliage brightens the border on its own.

common_name: Sunshine Blue II Bluebeard (Improved Gold-Leaf Caryopteris incana)

planting.note: Set out container-grown plants in spring in full sun and sharply drained soil; the improved hardiness of this selection lets it be grown as a reliable perennial shrub further north than older Caryopteris incana selections.

directions: Sunshine Blue II is a hardier improvement on the original Sunshine Blue caryopteris incana, bred for better winter survival and denser branching while keeping the same eye-catching combination of bright chartreuse-gold foliage and deep violet-blue flower clusters in late summer and fall. Because it is a Caryopteris incana selection rather than a x clandonensis hybrid, it blooms slightly later and tolerates heat exceptionally well, though it still benefits from a hard spring cutback to the base since flowers form on new growth. Plant in lean, fast-draining soil in full sun; the gold foliage colors best with strong light and struggles in shade or overly rich soil. Once established it is drought tolerant and attracts late-season pollinators when few other shrubs are still flowering.

common_name: Superba Russian Sage (Compact Silver-Leaf Perennial Plant of the Year)

planting.note: Plant in spring in poor to average, sharply drained soil; cut back hard to about 6 inches in early spring once new basal growth appears.

directions: Superba is one of the oldest named Russian sage selections in cultivation, honored as a Perennial Plant of the Year for its dependable performance, and remains valued for its fragrant, finely textured silver-green foliage and abundant lavender-blue flower spikes from midsummer through August. It grows slightly more branched and floriferous than unnamed seedling stock of the species. Grow in full sun and lean, well-drained soil, since fertile or damp ground causes weak, floppy stems and root rot; established plants shrug off heat, drought, and poor soil that would kill most other perennials. Leave the woody stems standing over winter for structure and crown protection, then cut back hard in early spring as new growth resumes from the base.
sources: Chicago Botanic Garden Plant Evaluation Notes

planting.note: Plant container-grown specimens in spring or fall in well-drained, average to poor soil in full sun to partial shade; give it the same generous spacing as the straight species.

directions: Marginata is a variegated selection of thorny elaeagnus distinguished by clean, silvery-white margins around each glossy green leaf, giving the dense evergreen canopy a brighter, more formal look than the species type while retaining the same tough, low-maintenance constitution. Small, intensely fragrant white flowers open in autumn and are followed by tart, edible red berries the following spring. Like the species it tolerates drought, salt spray, wind, and poor or alkaline soils once established, and it responds well to shearing if used as a hedge or screen, though hard pruning can encourage a flush of reverted, non-variegated shoots that should be cut out. Full sun brings out the strongest leaf contrast, while some afternoon shade is tolerated in hotter climates.

common_name: Compactum Bush Germander (Dwarf Silver Mediterranean Shrub)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in very well-drained, lean soil in full sun; damaged below about 15 degrees F, so best suited to zones 8-11.

directions: Compactum is a dwarf, dense-growing selection of bush germander that keeps the species' luminous silver-gray, woolly foliage and pale blue, two-lipped flowers in a tidy mounded form roughly a third the size of the straight species. Its neat habit makes it especially useful as a low informal or clipped hedge, edging, or foundation accent in Mediterranean and waterwise gardens where the full-size species would quickly outgrow the space. Grow in very well-drained, lean, neutral to alkaline soil in full sun; it is highly drought-tolerant once established but intolerant of wet or heavy soils. Shear lightly after the main spring-to-summer flowering flush to maintain its compact, rounded shape.
